A2.SS2.SSS2.2.normalized_reading_text: Proof. For $\lambda\geq 0$ , let $h_{\lambda}(x):=e^{-\lambda\|x\|^{2}}$ and define $H(\lambda):=\mathbb{E}\left[\det(O)\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}h_{\lambda}(x)p_{O}(x)\,dx\right].$ Since the two determinant components have Haar probability $1/2$ , $H(\lambda)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\mathbb{E}_{P_{+1}}h_{\lambda}-\mathbb{E}_{P_{-1}}h_{\lambda}\right).$ As $0<h_{\lambda}\leq 1$ , it follows that $\operatorname{TV}(P_{+1},P_{-1})\geq 2|H(\lambda)|.$ (20) We compute $H(\lambda)$ and then choose $\lambda>0$ . For every $Q\in O(n)$ , conjugation preserves Haar measure and the determinant sign, while $A_{QOQ^{\top}}=QA_{O}Q^{\top}$ and $p_{QOQ^{\top}}(Qx)=p_{O}(x)$ . Consequently, for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ , $\mathbb{E}[\det(O)p_{O}(x)]=\mathbb{E}[\det(O)p_{O}(\|x\|e_{1})].$ At $\|x\|e_{1}$ , the Gaussian exponent depends on $O$ only through $U$ , since $e_{1}^{\top}A_{O}e_{1}=(\kappa+1-(\kappa-1)U)/2$ . Moreover, $I_{n}\preceq A_{O}\preceq\kappa I_{n}$ gives the integrable bound $h_{\lambda}(x)p_{O}(\|x\|e_{1})\leq\left(\frac{\kappa}{2\pi}\right)^{n/2}e^{-\|x\|^{2}/2}.$ Using $|\det(O)|=1$ , Fubini’s theorem, and Gaussian integration, we obtain $\displaystyle H(\lambda)$ $\displaystyle=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{n/2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\det(O)\sqrt{\det A_{O}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}e^{-[\kappa+1+4\lambda-(\kappa-1)U]\|x\|^{2}/4}\,dx\right]$ $\displaystyle=2^{n/2}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{\det(O)\sqrt{\det A_{O}}}{(\kappa+1+4\lambda-(\kappa-1)U)^{n/2}}\right],$ where $\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}e^{-a\|x\|^{2}/4}\,dx=(4\pi/a)^{n/2}$ for $a>0$ . The denominator is at least $2+4\lambda$ , so Lemma B.6 applies with $h(u)=(\kappa+1+4\lambda-(\kappa-1)u)^{-n/2}$ and gives $H(\lambda)=\frac{(-1)^{n-1}(\sqrt{\kappa}-1)^{n-1}}{2^{n/2}}\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)U-(\sqrt{\kappa}-1)}{(\kappa+1+4\lambda-(\kappa-1)U)^{n/2}}\right].$ (21) Since $Oe_{1}$ is uniform on $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ , Lemma A.1 applies to $U$ . We now match the denominator with a positive multiple of $1+r^{2}-2rU$ . At $\lambda=0$ , this matching gives $r=(\sqrt{\kappa}-1)/(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)$ , but $H(0)=0$ because both target distributions have total mass one. We therefore decrease $r$ by a factor $1-1/n$ and set $\displaystyle r$ $\displaystyle:=\left(1-\frac{1}{n}\right)\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1},$ (22) $\displaystyle\lambda$ $\displaystyle:=\frac{\kappa-1}{8r}(1+r^{2})-\frac{\kappa+1}{4}=\frac{4n\sqrt{\kappa}+(\sqrt{\kappa}-1)^{2}}{8n(n-1)}.$ Then $0<r<1$ , $\lambda>0$ , and $\displaystyle\kappa+1+4\lambda-(\kappa-1)U$ $\displaystyle=\frac{\kappa-1}{2r}(1+r^{2}-2rU)$ (23) $\displaystyle=\frac{n(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^{2}}{2(n-1)}(1+r^{2}-2rU).$ The two Poisson identities yield $\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)U-(\sqrt{\kappa}-1)}{(1+r^{2}-2rU)^{n/2}}\right]$ $\displaystyle=\frac{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)r-(\sqrt{\kappa}-1)}{1-r^{2}}$ $\displaystyle=-\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{n(1-r^{2})}.$ Substitution into Eq. (21) gives $\displaystyle H(\lambda)$ $\displaystyle=\frac{(-1)^{n-1}(\sqrt{\kappa}-1)^{n-1}}{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^{n}}\left(1-\frac{1}{n}\right)^{n/2}\left(-\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{n(1-r^{2})}\right)$ (24) $\displaystyle=\frac{(-1)^{n}}{n}\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}\right)^{n}\frac{(1-1/n)^{n/2}}{1-r^{2}}.$ It remains to lower-bound the test gap. Since $n/2\geq 1$ , convexity of $t\mapsto t^{n/2}$ implies $\left(1-\frac{1}{n}\right)^{n/2}\geq 1-\frac{n}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{n}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Also, $\displaystyle n(1-r^{2})$ $\displaystyle=\frac{4n\sqrt{\kappa}}{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^{2}}+\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}\right)^{2}\left(2-\frac{1}{n}\right)$ $\displaystyle\leq\frac{4n\sqrt{\kappa}}{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^{2}}+2.$ Together with Eq. (20) and Eq. (24), these estimates give $\displaystyle\operatorname{TV}(P_{+1},P_{-1})$ $\displaystyle\geq\frac{2}{n}\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}\right)^{n}\frac{(1-1/n)^{n/2}}{1-r^{2}}$ $\displaystyle\geq\frac{\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}\right)^{n}}{2+\frac{4n\sqrt{\kappa}}{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^{2}}}.$ This proves the first claimed bound. For the second, $\kappa\geq 4$ implies $\displaystyle\log\left(\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}\right)$ $\displaystyle=2\int_{0}^{1/\sqrt{\kappa}}\frac{dt}{1-t^{2}}$ $\displaystyle\leq\frac{2}{\sqrt{\kappa}(1-\kappa^{-1})}\leq\frac{8}{3\sqrt{\kappa}}\leq\frac{3}{\sqrt{\kappa}}.$ Hence $((\sqrt{\kappa}-1)/(\sqrt{\kappa}+1))^{n}\geq e^{-3n/\sqrt{\kappa}}$ . Using $1+t\leq e^{t}$ , we also have $2+\frac{4n\sqrt{\kappa}}{(\sqrt{\kappa}+1)^{2}}\leq 2+\frac{4n}{\sqrt{\kappa}}\leq 2e^{2n/\sqrt{\kappa}}.$ Therefore, $\operatorname{TV}(P_{+1},P_{-1})\geq\frac{e^{-3n/\sqrt{\kappa}}}{2e^{2n/\sqrt{\kappa}}}=\frac{1}{2}e^{-5n/\sqrt{\kappa}}.$ ∎

A2.SS2.SSS3.2.normalized_reading_text: Proof of Lemma 3.3. Let $a$ denote the single-block Hellinger affinity: $a:=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}\sqrt{p_{+1}(x)p_{-1}(x)}\,dx.$ Cauchy–Schwarz and $\int p_{+1}=\int p_{-1}=1$ give $0\leq a\leq 1$ and $\displaystyle\operatorname{TV}(P_{+1},P_{-1})$ $\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}|\sqrt{p_{+1}}-\sqrt{p_{-1}}|(\sqrt{p_{+1}}+\sqrt{p_{-1}})$ $\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{2}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}(\sqrt{p_{+1}}-\sqrt{p_{-1}})^{2}\right)^{1/2}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}(\sqrt{p_{+1}}+\sqrt{p_{-1}})^{2}\right)^{1/2}$ $\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{(2-2a)(2+2a)}=\sqrt{1-a^{2}}.$ Proposition B.7 therefore implies $a\leq\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{4}e^{-10n/\sqrt{\kappa}}}\leq\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{8}e^{-10n/\sqrt{\kappa}}\right\},$ (25) where the last inequality follows from $\log(1-t)\leq-t$ for $0\leq t<1$ . Let $\bar{p}_{b}$ be the density of $\bar{\pi}_{b}$ . When $kn<d$ , write $\varphi_{d-kn}$ for the standard Gaussian density on $\mathbb{R}^{d-kn}$ . By Eq. (6), $\bar{p}_{b}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{k},z)=\prod_{j=1}^{k}p_{b}(x_{j})\,\varphi_{d-kn}(z).$ Tonelli’s theorem and $\int\varphi_{d-kn}=1$ give $\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\sqrt{\bar{p}_{+1}(x)\bar{p}_{-1}(x)}\,dx$ $\displaystyle=\prod_{j=1}^{k}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}\sqrt{p_{+1}(x_{j})p_{-1}(x_{j})}\,dx_{j}\right)\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d-kn}}\varphi_{d-kn}(z)\,dz$ $\displaystyle=a^{k}.$ When $kn=d$ , the same identity holds with the Gaussian factor omitted. Finally, $\min\{u,v\}\leq\sqrt{uv}$ for $u,v\geq 0$ implies $\displaystyle\operatorname{TV}(\bar{\pi}_{+1},\bar{\pi}_{-1})$ $\displaystyle=1-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\min\{\bar{p}_{+1}(x),\bar{p}_{-1}(x)\}\,dx$ $\displaystyle\geq 1-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\sqrt{\bar{p}_{+1}(x)\bar{p}_{-1}(x)}\,dx$ $\displaystyle=1-a^{k}$ $\displaystyle\geq 1-\exp\left\{-\frac{k}{8}e^{-10n/\sqrt{\kappa}}\right\},$ where the last step uses Eq. (25). ∎
